C-SECTIONS-PLUGIN-V2.Summary: One product name: the repository review that was built as a second skill is folded into smart-review, which becomes a plugin made of sections, with an upgrade path for installs made before the plugin.
C-SECTIONS-PLUGIN-V2.Problem: The scored repository review shipped as a separate skill with its own name, CLI name, artifact directory, and guidance file, beside the diff review. Users met two names for one tool and had to know which skill a request belongs to. The maintainer decided that smart-review absorbs the functionality and grows by sections, including future ones for live sites, with one command per section and a default that runs everything applicable.

Goals.Goal: A single skill directory skills/smart-review holds the dispatcher, the changes workflow (the former diff review), the repository workflow for scored sections, all agents, rubrics, references, schemas, and the CLI.
The unit of work is a section everywhere: findings documents, run metadata, CLI flags, lint rule names, reports in English and Russian, documentation.
The plugin exposes one command per section plus full, quick, and update; with no section named, every applicable section runs after the plan is shown.
The CLI, the artifact directory, the guidance file, and the package use the product name: smart-review, .smart-review/, SMART_REVIEW.md, @xronocode/smart-review.
Version 2.0.0 in the package, the CLI, and both plugin manifests, with an upgrade section in README and CHANGELOG.

Constraints.Constraint: The skill name stays smart-review so that an existing install made with the skills installer upgrades in place.

The behaviour of the diff review is preserved inside the changes section; only its modes full, full+errors, and full-project are renamed to standard, standard+errors, and project, and the old names stay understood as modes of that section.
Scoring, lint rules' meaning, rubric content, and rubric versions do not change; only names do.
Nothing is published, pushed, or tagged by this change; the package stays private.

NonGoals.NonGoal: New sections (live-site security, SEO, usability); the structure only makes them additive.
Converting run directories written by the unreleased pre-rename CLI.
Fixing the upstream links of the changes section that were already dead.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: No tracked file outside .grace/changes/archive names the former second skill, its CLI, its directory, or its guidance file.
make validate fails when a rubric has no command file or no row in the SKILL.md sections table, when the skill name changes, or when the manifests and the package disagree on the version.
make test passes with the renamed fields, flags, and rule names; the example report is regenerated by the renamed CLI and passes lint.
The skills installer installs the skill from the local path into a clean directory and the installed CLI runs score and lint.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Both commands exit zero; the example build prints a passing lint; a search of tracked files for the former names returns nothing outside the archive.

Assumptions.Assumption: The scored review was never released, so renaming its CLI, fields, directory, and guidance file breaks no user.
Graph modules are renamed from M-AUDIT-* to M-SECTION-* together with their verification entries; archived bundles keep the names they were written with.

The maintainer approved the direction, the product-name choice for CLI and files, and version 2.0.0 in conversation; the mode renames and the name inspector for the per-section agent are implementation defaults.
